comments.text:
Albums that made me love vinyl records: 
Jane's Addiction - "Stop"/"Three Days" 12'' vinyl single - found mine at a garage sale around 1995 or 1996. Prior to that, I already knew the band very well but that single took the music on it to a different place.
Neil Young - After The Gold Rush - I got my copy when I rescued it from my mother's parents' house (my uncle bought it new long before I was born nd left it there until I found it), and it began my love of Young's music which endures to this day, forty years on.
LIGHT//SOUND's self-titled album featured music which wasn't bad -- 100% indie rock, but the cover is wild. Made from floorboards re-purposed from houses that were demolished by Hurricane Katrina, the album cover is unlike anything I'd seen before or since. I've kept my copyin as good and safe a shape and place as I can, but it is slowly crumbling because of its nature. Ultimately, it proves that even if you take care of it, time will take something from you.
My copy of Johnny Cash's Live at Folsom Prison was purchased new by my grandfather, long before I was born. Ironically, he didn't like the album very much (a bigger fan of Hank Snow), but it remainded unplayed among his records, and I found it when I was helping to pack up his things after he died. It's very possible that I've listened to it more than he ever did. On a similar tip -- 
My copy of The Beatles' "Daytripper" b/w "We Can Work It Out" 7'' single was purchased new by my father's best friend when it was released in the Sixties. He brought it over to my father's house when they were getting ready to go somewhere and left it there when they left. My father never liked The Beatles (yeah yeah yeah) so his friend forgot about it and Dad never played it. It got packed into storage and moved every time my father moved until I found it in that box, in the Nineties. By then, my father's best friend had been dead for a decade and dad still didn't like The Beatles, so he gave it to me -- and I still have it, in like new condition.

In each case, the story means as much to me as the music.
comments.author: @BillAdams-fb3jm

comments.text:
I was a teen and unable to grasp the musical revolution I was in the middle of; tooth and nail, alternative rock, and artists still making the album as a whole an experience instead of singles surrounded by filler. And getting hooked on the vinyl experience I’ve really been grabbing onto my corner.

Phoenix 10 year - The Classic Crime; 2 disc vinyl release perfectly separated and led into with all 4 sides with wide grooves to accommodate the hot mix. Beautiful gatefold, letter from the band, and the album was mastered and ordered with a flow that makes you finish it every time.

Colliding By Design - Acceptance; their comeback from a criminal treatment by their original label and produced with Aaron Sprinkle. I was in love streaming it in 2017, and even more with their opaque red vinyl release. Beautiful blend of 80s influence and modern alt themes with amazing melodics; vinyl makes it even better.

Never Take a Friendship Personal 20 Year - Anberlin; it took this to another level on this medium. The sound was remastered for the vinyl and everything was tighter and more articulate than the original. And instead of a wall of sound when the dynamics went big, with the vinyl they tempered it. Instead it’s like the sound blooms into a chorus or breakdown that feels like a fresh cup of water. Perfect.

Phantazia - Noel Pointer. Was listening to “the greatest jazz recordings of all time” from the Franklin mint company on their “strings” volume and “Night Song” was on side A of one of them. It’s his violin jazz/funk stuff. I immediately hunted for and bought a mint pressing from 1977 of his debut album. It’s a stunning work, blending funk and jazz elements together with beautiful experiments that I can’t find anywhere else. I play it at least 2-3 times a week, and it’s a treat every time
comments.author: @jacobblankenship5655

My first record, Out of the blue from ELO, if I remember well, it came with a cardboard "kit" to build the spaceship.
I have Deja Vu from CSN&Y. That is a thick cardboard sleeve that feels like leather and there is a real black and white picture glued on there. I bought it used for almost nothing second hand, I think back in the late 70's. I bought a night at the opera from queen when it was just released and it is white vinyl, I had never seen that before (back then)
I just bought Parasomnia from Dream theater. The vinyl is much thicker than the average 80's records, the sleeve has beautiful artwork and it came with a booklet full of the same sort of art. that is for me one of the things why I like vinyl, it is the whole experience from taking it out the sleeve, put the sleeve in front of me, clean the record. Then when the needle touches the vinyl you get the typical ticking sounds that trigger good memories.

comments.text:
I started my journey in the early to mid-80's at the tail end of the first wave of the vinyl generation, and subsequently fell heavily into the CD collection process for the next 35 years until COVID arrived and boredom re-ignited my journey down the rabbit hole of vinyl collection again.
If I were to throw 5 albums (or maybe better to say 5 artists) into the mix that have pretty much driven my love for the format they would be:
- Split Enz "True Colours (several copies with the different album art colours but especially my copy with the holographic vinyl that reflects a little like a laser show in the right light and angle of light). The Finn  brothers both brought their A game to this record with any number of hits and should have been hits.
- Spandau Ballet "True" / Ultravox "Vienna" / ABC "Lexicon of Love". I was an '80's teen adult and abosultely love the "New Romantic" sound. They once said how boring the '80s was for music and now they would be eating their words with a plethera of artists all re-engaing both older and in many cases younger audiences with nostalgic tours.
- The Beloved "Happiness". I bought this one originally on CD bacnk in the ealr 90's and was very disappointed with the mixing and mastering with the volume set very low and the beats almost lost in the compression. Then I recently came across a test pressing of the album on vinyl and OMFG!!!!! (you can decide whether I was blown away or  not).
And an honourable mention from the current new artist:
- Ha Vay "Baby I'm The Wolf. An almost Kate Bush-like experience on record by a very new and talented artist who complimented her release with a full blown (home-made) concept video of the entire record. The songs have a folk-pop ethereal feel to them that draw you into the world of imagination inside this artist's mind.
comments.author: @heartlikeasky6532

comments.text: A bootleg copy of the Norman Haines Band - den of Inequity - original pressings @ £500+ being beyond my pay grade had me captivated by the grotesque Edwardian cartoon sleeve. This opened my ears to a new genre - but the grandfather of my collection was the self titled debut album by Queen - the record released in 73 had sat on the shelf at Martin's newagents for years and captivated my imagination when looking at the rear sleeve montage artwork. In 1979, aged 9, I saved my 99p and finally bought it - took it home and listened to it on my parents aging dansette player, and I was spellbound.

comments.text:
I started my journey in the early to mid-80's at the tail end of the first wave of the vinyl generation, and subsequently fell heavily into the CD collection process for the next 35 years until COVID arrived and boredom re-ignited my journey down the rabbit hole of vinyl collection again.
If I were to throw 5 albums (or maybe better to say 5 artists) into the mix that have pretty much driven my love for the format they would be:
- Split Enz "True Colours (several copies with the different album art colours but especially my copy with the holographic vinyl that reflects a little like a laser show in the right light and angle of light). The Finn  brothers both brought their A game to this record with any number of hits and should have been hits.
- Spandau Ballet "True" / Ultravox "Vienna" / ABC "Lexicon of Love". I was an '80's teen adult and abosultely love the "New Romantic" sound. They once said how boring the '80s was for music and now they would be eating their words with a plethera of artists all re-engaing both older and in many cases younger audiences with nostalgic tours.
- The Beloved "Happiness". I bought this one originally on CD bacnk in the ealr 90's and was very disappointed with the mixing and mastering with the volume set very low and the beats almost lost in the compression. Then I recently came across a test pressing of the album on vinyl and OMFG!!!!! (you can decide whether I was blown away or  not).
And an honourable mention from the current new artist:
- Ha Vay "Baby I'm The Wolf. An almost Kate Bush-like experience on record by a very new and talented artist who complimented her release with a full blown (home-made) concept video of the entire record. The songs have a folk-pop ethereal feel to them that draw you into the world of imagination inside this artist's mind.
comments.author: @heartlikeasky6532

comments.text: The list of records that "belong" on vinyl, have great music and cool, artistic covers is long. To name a few: The Beatles "White Album", ELO "Out of the Blue", Alice Cooper "School's Out", Split Enz "True Colors" with laser etched vinyl, Pink Floyd- DSOTM or The Wall, Led Zeppelin-Physical Graffiti, Elton John-Goodbye Yellow Brick Road. The Japanese really outdid themselves back in the 60s/70s, with lots of extra "goodies" that weren't found on LPs in other countries, not to mention their incredible "Everclean" red-vinyl pressings made from dead quiet virgin vinyl.
comments.author: @jeffreylind3739

comments.text: I would add Dave Mason’s “Alone Together” which was the first album I purchased that wasn’t pressed on black vinyl. Instead it came on an interesting marbled finish. The jacket, if you chose, could be hung as an interesting mobile which is how it was displayed at the record shop where it was purchased. The songs, musicianship, and sound quality are all very good.
